title: Nephi makes and engraves plates of ore
summary: Nephi makes plates of ore and engraves his father's record, their wilderness journeyings, his father's prophecies, and many of his own prophecies upon them. He says the first plates contain a more particular account of events before he made these plates.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord commanded Nephi, and Nephi made plates of ore to engrave the record of his people.
Nephi engraved his father's record, their wilderness journeyings, his father's prophecies, and many of his own prophecies upon the plates he made.
When Nephi made the first plates, he did not know he would be commanded to make these plates.

The first plates contain his father's record, the genealogy of his father's fathers, and most of their wilderness proceedings; events before Nephi made these plates are recorded there more particularly.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephi making plates of ore and engraving them.
unspecified_visual_details: Nephi's appearance, his tools, the surroundings, and the plates' precise design.

narration.text: wherefore I did make plates of ore

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Nephi is the first-person narrator. The first plates are discussed as an earlier record, not as a simultaneous event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the Lord appearing; no appearance is described.
Do not invent a specific location or workshop.
Do not depict the earlier wilderness proceedings as occurring while Nephi makes these plates.

title: The plates’ purpose
summary: Nephi recounts receiving a commandment about what should be written on the plates and why it should be kept. He says he made a record on other plates concerning his people’s wars, contentions, and destructions, and gave instructions for after he was gone. He says an account of making these plates will be given later.

explicit_facts.text: After making these plates, Nephi received a commandment to write the more plain and precious parts of the ministry and prophecies on them and keep the writings for his people’s instruction and other wise purposes known to the Lord.
Nephi made a record on other plates giving a greater account of his people’s wars, contentions, and destructions.
Nephi commanded his people what to do after he was gone and said the plates should be handed down from generation to generation, or prophet to prophet, until further commandments of the Lord.
Nephi says an account of making these plates will be given later and that he proceeds as he has spoken so the more sacred things may be kept for his people’s knowledge.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephi may be shown with plates while his retrospective account appears as narration; the reported events need not be staged.
unspecified_visual_details: Nephi’s appearance and clothing, the plates’ appearance, and the setting.

narration.text: I, Nephi, did make a record upon the other plates,
and this I do that the more sacred things may be kept for the knowledge of my people.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The commandment and the record on the other plates are reported retrospectively. No divine appearance is described.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the Lord appearing or add dialogue from him.
Do not stage the wars, destructions, or later handing down of the plates as present events.

title: What Is Sacred and What Is Set at Naught
summary: Nephi says he writes upon plates only what he thinks sacred and acknowledges his weakness. He says some people set at naught what others value and do not hearken to God's counsels.

explicit_facts.text: Nephi says he writes nothing upon plates unless he thinks it sacred and acknowledges his weakness according to the flesh.
Nephi says some people set at naught what others consider valuable and do not hearken to God's counsels.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Plates may be shown as the object Nephi refers to, without depicting a specific act of writing underway.

narration.text: Nevertheless, I do not write anything upon plates save it be that I think it be sacred.
For the things which some men esteem to be of great worth, both to the body and soul, others set at naught and trample under their feet.
they set him at naught, and hearken not to the voice of his counsels.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The trampling language is figurative, not a narrated physical event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict God as a visible figure; no appearance is described.
Do not depict literal trampling of God.
Do not invent Nephi's appearance or surroundings as facts.

title: A prophecy of his coming and suffering
summary: Nephi reports that the one prophesied of will come six hundred years after his father left Jerusalem. He prophesies that the world will judge that person a thing of naught, scourge, smite, and spit upon him, and that he will suffer it.

explicit_facts.text: According to the words of the angel, the one prophesied of will come six hundred years after Nephi’s father left Jerusalem.
The world will judge him to be a thing of naught, scourge and smite him, and he will suffer it.
They will spit upon him, and he will suffer it because of his loving kindness and long-suffering towards the children of men.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephi may be depicted as the source of the account without depicting the prophesied events as occurring in his present.
unspecified_visual_details: Nephi’s appearance, posture, activity, and location; the appearance of the one prophesied of; the identities and appearances of those who will mistreat him.

narration.text: And behold he cometh, according to the words of the angel, in six hundred years from the time my father left Jerusalem.
And the world, because of their iniquity, shall judge him to be a thing of naught;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Nephi reports a prophecy about someone else; the predicted mistreatment is not occurring in Nephi’s present.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Nephi as the one who comes or suffers.
Do not depict the predicted mistreatment as a present event.
Do not invent an appearance for the one prophesied of or identities for those who mistreat him.

title: Prophecy of crucifixion and darkness
summary: The verse says the God of the fathers yields himself as a man into the hands of wicked men, to be lifted up, crucified, and buried in a sepulchre. It says three days of darkness should be a sign of his death to inhabitants of the isles of the sea, especially those of the house of Israel.

explicit_facts.text: The God of the fathers, also called the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, yields himself as a man into the hands of wicked men, to be lifted up, crucified, and buried in a sepulchre, according to the words of the angel, Zenock, Neum, and Zenos.
Three days of darkness should be a sign of his death to those inhabiting the isles of the sea, especially those of the house of Israel.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The verse may be presented as written or spoken prophecy without depicting the prophesied events as happening.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearance, identity, and setting of any person presenting the prophecy are unspecified.
The appearance of the God of the fathers and the wicked men, and the settings of the prophesied events, are unspecified.

narration.text: yieldeth himself, according to the words of the angel, as a man, into the hands of wicked men
to be lifted up, according to the words of Zenock, and to be crucified
and to be buried in a sepulchre, according to the words of Zenos

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verse reports what is to happen and cites earlier prophetic words; it does not narrate these events as happening in the present.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the crucifixion, burial, or three days of darkness as present events.
Do not depict an angel or invent appearances for figures not described.

title: Prophecy of signs and upheaval
summary: A prophet foretells that the Lord God will visit the house of Israel in different ways. Zenos says the foretold events and the rending of rocks must come, and that many kings of the isles of the sea will be moved to exclaim that the God of nature suffers.
characters: Kings of the isles of the sea (mentioned)

explicit_facts.text: The Lord God will visit all the house of Israel; some will hear his voice because of their righteousness, unto joy and salvation, while others will experience signs of his power.
The foretold signs include thunderings, lightnings, tempest, fire, smoke, vapor of darkness, the opening of the earth, and mountains carried up.
Zenos says these things must come and the rocks of the earth must rend.
Because of the groanings of the earth, many kings of the isles of the sea will be wrought upon by the Spirit of God to exclaim that the God of nature suffers.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Present the passage as prophecy, not as events occurring in the narrator’s present.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearance of the Lord God, the identities and appearances of the kings, and specific locations are not given.

narration.text: And the rocks of the earth must rend;
The God of nature suffers.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The kings’ exclamation is foretold, not narrated as speech occurring in the present scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show the predicted signs as occurring in the narrator’s present.
Do not invent the Lord God’s visible appearance or identify the prophet speaking in verse 11.

title: Prophecy concerning Jerusalem
summary: The prophet says those at Jerusalem will be scourged by all people because they crucify the God of Israel and turn their hearts aside, rejecting signs and wonders and God's power and glory. They will wander in the flesh, perish, become a hiss and a byword, and be hated among all nations.

explicit_facts.text: The prophet says those at Jerusalem will be scourged by all people because they crucify the God of Israel and turn their hearts aside, rejecting signs and wonders and the power and glory of the God of Israel.
The prophet says they will wander in the flesh, perish, become a hiss and a byword, and be hated among all nations because they turn their hearts aside and despise the Holy One of Israel.

unspecified_visual_details: Whether any person or location is visually represented.
The appearance of any people or places.

narration.text: they shall wander in the flesh, and perish,

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verses present these events as prophecy; they do not narrate their fulfillment as a present scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the prophesied scourging, wandering, or persecution as present events.
Do not invent a visible appearance for the God of Israel or the Holy One of Israel.

title: Promises to the House of Israel
summary: The prophecy says that when they no more turn aside their hearts against the Holy One of Israel, he will remember the covenants made to their fathers, remember the isles of the sea, and gather in the house of Israel from the four quarters of the earth. All the earth shall see the Lord’s salvation, and every nation, kindred, tongue, and people shall be blessed.

explicit_facts.text: When they no more turn aside their hearts against the Holy One of Israel, he will remember the covenants he made to their fathers.
He will remember the isles of the sea and gather in all the people who are of the house of Israel from the four quarters of the earth, according to the words of the prophet Zenos.
All the earth shall see the salvation of the Lord, and every nation, kindred, tongue, and people shall be blessed.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The promises may be presented as prophecy rather than as events occurring now.
unspecified_visual_details: How or when the promised gathering occurs.
The setting and any people depicted.

narration.text: then will he remember the covenants which he made to their fathers
Yea, then will he remember the isles of the sea
will I gather in
from the four quarters of the earth
all the earth shall see the salvation of the Lord
every nation, kindred, tongue and people shall be blessed

doctrinal_or_story_notes: These verses state promised future events; they do not narrate the gathering as occurring in the present.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the promised gathering or salvation as a present event.
Do not invent the Lord’s appearance, a setting, or unnamed individuals.

title: Nephi's purpose and burden
summary: Nephi says he has written to persuade his people to remember the Lord their Redeemer and speaks to all the house of Israel if they obtain these things. He describes spiritual workings that weary him for those at Jerusalem and says the Lord mercifully showed him concerning them. He says the Lord showed prophets of old concerning them and many concerning his own people, and that these things are written on the plates of brass.

explicit_facts.text: Nephi says he has written these things to persuade his people to remember the Lord their Redeemer.
Nephi speaks to all the house of Israel, if they should obtain these things.
Nephi says workings in the spirit weary him and weaken all his joints for those at Jerusalem. He says the Lord mercifully showed him concerning them and that otherwise he would have perished also.
Nephi says the Lord showed prophets of old things concerning those at Jerusalem and showed many concerning his own people; these things are written on the plates of brass.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephi's posture may suggest the weariness and weakness he describes.
unspecified_visual_details: Nephi's appearance, precise expression, and setting are unspecified.
The text does not describe what Nephi was shown or a visible appearance of the Lord.

narration.text: And I, Nephi, have written these things unto my people, that perhaps I might persuade them that they would remember the Lord their Redeemer.
Wherefore, I speak unto all the house of Israel,
I have workings in the spirit, which doth weary me even that all my joints are weak,
for they are written upon the plates of brass.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Nephi reports what the Lord showed him and others; no visible appearance is described.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict an invented vision or appearance of the Lord.
Do not show people at Jerusalem or prophets of old as physically present with Nephi.
Do not portray the plates of brass as necessarily the record Nephi is writing here.

title: Nephi teaches his brethren
summary: Nephi teaches his brethren and reads to them from the plates of brass, the books of Moses, and the prophet Isaiah. He likens all scriptures to them for their profit and learning.

explicit_facts.text: Nephi teaches his brethren and reads many things engraved on the plates of brass to them, that they might know of the Lord's doings in other lands among people of old.

Nephi reads things written in the books of Moses and the prophet Isaiah to persuade his brethren to believe in the Lord their Redeemer, and likens all scriptures to them for their profit and learning.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephi is reading from the plates of brass while his brethren listen.
unspecified_visual_details: The number and individual identities of Nephi's brethren, their appearance, and the setting.

narration.text: Now it came to pass that I, Nephi, did teach my brethren these things;
for I did liken all scriptures unto us, that it might be for our profit and learning.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The specific content of the readings from the plates of brass, Moses, and Isaiah is not given in these verses.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict events or teachings from the books of Moses or Isaiah beyond what these verses state.
Do not identify Nephi's brethren individually.

title: Nephi addresses his brethren
summary: Nephi tells his brethren, who are a remnant of the house of Israel and a broken-off branch, to hear the prophet's words and liken them to themselves so they may have hope.

explicit_facts.text: Nephi speaks to his brethren, calling them a remnant of the house of Israel and a branch that has been broken off.
Nephi tells them to hear the prophet's words and liken them to themselves so they may have hope.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephi is addressing the gathered brethren.
unspecified_visual_details: The setting, the brethren's appearance, and their reactions.
